candidateDecisions.label: Chemistry, physics, biobased materials and nanomaterials

analysis: The closest plan sustains life science through molecular cell biology, metabolism, genetics and laboratory experiments, and Earth systems through geology, biogeochemistry, climate, spatial analysis and Earth system modeling. Marine Biology and Earth Observation give field and spatial methods in place of the unsuitable early research-project offering and broaden ecosystem evidence in place of physiology. The neuroscience option prioritises brain, cognition, language and biomedical function; statistics and evidence synthesis support its methods. The quantitative life-science option prioritises signals, numerical analysis, imaging and machine learning as transferable methods alongside physiology and molecular biology, with no implied specialist bioengineering qualification. Sustainability Essentials I covers real physical, chemical and materials concepts in applied contexts; Biochemistry and Environmental Biogeochemistry extend chemistry in selected domains. Neither sustained disciplinary chemistry/physics nor a materials-science pathway is supported. Core chemistry correspondence is partial and introductory physics, philosophy of science and the collaborative core project have no adequate one-to-one counterparts. General education and profile choices are kept open. Optional independent research does not count toward 180 scheduled EC.

alignment.rationale: Both introduce the biology of living systems. UCR emphasizes molecules, cells and human biology.
Maastricht introduces general chemistry. UCR Biochemistry covers chemical processes in living organisms.
Maastricht requires introductory physics. UCR applies selected physical principles in sustainability and Earth science courses.
Both develop experimental skills. UCR’s laboratory course emphasizes biochemical and molecular methods.
Both develop experimental design and data analysis. Maastricht applies them in a dedicated laboratory skills course.
Maastricht integrates the core courses through a collaborative literature review and poster presentation.
Maastricht teaches philosophy and communication of science in a dedicated course.
Maastricht requires one mathematics choice. UCR develops mathematics across several scheduled courses.
Maastricht requires one approved humanities or social-science course.
Maastricht students choose courses for their own science profile. The three UCR plans illustrate distinct combinations.
Maastricht students choose eight additional skills modules. UCR teaches related methods within its scheduled courses.
Maastricht students complete four additional research projects in dedicated project periods.
Maastricht requires a 30 EC thesis. UCR independent research is optional and sits outside the scheduled degree.
